Q0_s1.explanation: The unit responds to dog faces, especially the snout, nose and mouth area, and it fires most strongly on small to medium, often fluffy or shaggy breeds seen face-on.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to dog faces, especially the snout, nose and mouth area, and it fires most strongly on small to medium, often fluffy or shaggy breeds seen face-on.
parsed.evidence: All 20 top photos are dogs with the box on the muzzle and nose, covering several breeds (terriers, a papillon, a Bernese, a Swiss mountain dog). In the random sample, only the photo with small dogs gets moderate activation (3), and unrelated scenes stay at 0-2.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on other furry animals' faces (cats, bears, foxes) and on non-face dog parts would show whether it is dog-specific or responds to snouts and muzzles in general.

F1_s1.explanation: The unit responds to a front-facing, roughly symmetric arrangement of a small, dark, glossy rounded blob centered below two smaller dark spots, set within soft, fine, wispy textured surroundings. It responds most when this arrangement is seen straight on at close-to-medium scale.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to a front-facing, roughly symmetric arrangement of a small, dark, glossy rounded blob centered below two smaller dark spots, set within soft, fine, wispy textured surroundings. It responds most when this arrangement is seen straight on at close-to-medium scale.
parsed.evidence: All 20 top activations (6–10) place the red box on this same centered dark-blob-and-spots arrangement, regardless of overall color, framing or background. Random photos without it score 0–2, and the highest random score (3) is the one containing several small instances of the same arrangement.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on the same arrangement without the surrounding soft texture (e.g., smooth or cropped versions), and on soft texture alone without the arrangement, to separate which part drives the response.
